jobs.prompt: Minimalist, cohesive video game screenshot of 'War Table', a calm world-conquest strategy board game in the spirit of classic Risk: a recognizable world map (the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia) divided into territories owned by four players. Design rules: extreme restraint and generous negative space; ONE line weight for all coastlines and borders; ownership shown only as a soft, low-saturation watercolor wash inside each territory; exactly ONE mark per territory: a small number set in an elegant serif inside a hairline circle; no soldier figures, no seals, no fake characters, no decorative scenery clutter; one elegant high-contrast serif typeface (like Cormorant Garamond) for all text; gold used only as hairline accents and for the single active element; small ring ornaments with a center dot as the recurring motif. Everything must feel like one cohesive design system, like a beautifully simple premium app. Tall portrait 9:19.5 smartphone screenshot of the same game: the map fills the screen with plenty of breathing room, four tiny player dots with counts at the top, and at the bottom a soft rounded pill control 'Place  Attack  Fortify  End' plus one 'Blitz' button. Variant: night ink. Deep navy ground (#1b2230) with a subtle fine grain; coastlines in thin warm-ivory hairlines; ownership as soft luminous low-saturation tints (muted coral, slate blue, pale gold, sage) glowing gently inside borders; gold hairline accents and ring ornaments with a center dot; sea routes as fine dotted gold lines. Ivory serif text. Quiet, elegant, like a star chart. High detail, premium, readable, no watermark.
